nodes.summary: The map `(α, τ) ↦ (α / D, 2 (1 - α) / D)` is a bijection from `{0 < α ≤ 1, 0 < τ}` onto `{0 < b, 0 ≤ δ < 1}`.
nodes.title: Purity and ploidy are identifiable from the slope and intercept of Eq. 1

nodes.summary: Doubling every copy number and the ploidy and replacing the purity by `α / (2 - α)` reproduces every copy ratio (the `m = 2` case of `copyRatio_scale`).
nodes.title: Genome doubling

nodes.summary: `R = (α / D) q + 2 (1 - α) / D`, for all real arguments.
nodes.title: Eq. 1 is affine in `q`

nodes.summary: Scaling every copy number and the ploidy by `m > 0` and the purity to `α / (m - (m - 1) α)` leaves every copy ratio of Eq. 1 unchanged.
nodes.title: Ploidy-scaling non-identifiability, copy ratios

nodes.summary: Relative copy ratio `R = (α q + 2 (1 - α)) / (α τ + 2 (1 - α))` of a locus with copy number `q`, purity `α` and cancer-cell ploidy `τ` (Carter et al. 2012, Eq. 1).
nodes.title: Relative copy ratio

nodes.summary: Ploidy-scaling non-identifiability, germline allelic fractions (Eq. 11): with copy number and germline multiplicity both scaled by `m > 0` and the purity rescaled, the allelic fraction is unchanged.
nodes.title: Ploidy-scaling non-identifiability, germline allelic fractions

nodes.summary: Expected allelic fraction `((1 - α) + α g) / (α q + 2 (1 - α))` of a heterozygous germline variant present in `g` copies per cancer cell at a locus of copy number `q` (Carter et al. 2012, Eq. 11).
nodes.title: Expected allelic fraction of a germline variant

nodes.summary: The copy-ratio intercept `2 (1 - α) / D` of Eq. 1 (Carter et al. 2012), the copy ratio of a homozygously deleted locus.
nodes.title: Copy-ratio intercept

nodes.summary: The mixture copy number is positive in the biological domain `0 ≤ α ≤ 1`, `0 < q`.
nodes.title: Positivity of the mixture copy number

nodes.summary: Average absolute copy number `α q + 2 (1 - α)` of a locus with copy number `q` in the cancer cells, in a sample of purity `α` whose normal cells are diploid (Carter et al. 2012). With `q = τ` this is the sample ploidy `D` of Eq. 1; with the local copy number it is `D_s` of Eq. 2.
nodes.title: Average absolute copy number of a tumor sample

nodes.summary: Inverse of Eq. 1, ploidy: `τ = (1 - δ) / b` for the slope `b` and intercept `δ`, when `0 < α ≤ 1` and `0 < τ`.
nodes.title: Ploidy from copy-ratio slope and intercept

nodes.summary: Inverse of Eq. 1, purity: `α = 2 b / (2 b + δ)` for the slope `b` and intercept `δ`, when `0 < α ≤ 1` and `0 < τ`.
nodes.title: Purity from copy-ratio slope and intercept

nodes.summary: The denominator `m - (m - 1) α = m (1 - α) + α` of the rescaled purity is positive for `m > 0` and `0 ≤ α ≤ 1`.
nodes.title: Positivity of the rescaled purity denominator

nodes.summary: The rescaled purity is again a purity: `0 ≤ α / (m - (m - 1) α) ≤ 1` for `m > 0` and `0 ≤ α ≤ 1`.
nodes.title: Rescaled purity lies in (0, 1)

nodes.summary: The rescaled solution is a genuinely different purity: for `0 < α < 1` and `m ≠ 1`, `α / (m - (m - 1) α) ≠ α`.
nodes.title: Rescaled purity differs from the original purity

nodes.summary: The purity `α / (m - (m - 1) α)` that, together with all copy numbers multiplied by `m`, reproduces the copy ratios and allelic fractions of purity `α` (derived from Carter et al. 2012, Eqs. 1, 2, 11).
nodes.title: Rescaled purity

nodes.summary: The copy-ratio slope `α / D` of Eq. 1 (Carter et al. 2012), the copy ratio of one extra copy per cancer cell.
nodes.title: Copy-ratio slope

nodes.summary: The somatic allelic fraction decreases with the local copy number (`0 ≤ α ≤ 1`, `0 ≤ s`, `0 < q ≤ q'`).
nodes.title: Somatic allelic fraction decreases with copy number

nodes.summary: Allelic fractions are determined by the copy-ratio slope (Carter et al. 2012, Eq. 2): `α s / D_s = (α / D) s / R`, whenever `D ≠ 0`.
nodes.title: Allelic fractions are determined by the copy-ratio slope

nodes.summary: A somatic allelic fraction is at most one when the multiplicity does not exceed the copy number (`s ≤ q`).
nodes.title: Somatic allelic fraction is at most one

nodes.summary: The somatic allelic fraction increases with the multiplicity (`0 ≤ α ≤ 1`, `0 < q`).
nodes.title: Somatic allelic fraction increases with multiplicity

nodes.summary: The somatic allelic fraction increases with the purity (`0 ≤ s`, `0 < q`).
nodes.title: Somatic allelic fraction increases with purity

nodes.summary: Somatic allelic fractions are nonnegative in the biological domain.
nodes.title: Nonnegativity of somatic allelic fractions

nodes.summary: Ploidy-scaling non-identifiability, somatic allelic fractions (Eq. 2): with copy number and multiplicity both scaled by `m > 0` and the purity rescaled, the allelic fraction is unchanged.
nodes.title: Ploidy-scaling non-identifiability, somatic allelic fractions

nodes.summary: Expected allelic fraction `α s / (α q + 2 (1 - α))` of a clonal somatic point mutation with multiplicity `s` (copies per cancer cell) at a locus of copy number `q` (Carter et al. 2012, Eq. 2; Eq. 10 is `s = 1`).
nodes.title: Expected allelic fraction of a somatic mutation

nodes.summary: If the segment weights `w` sum to one and the ploidy is the weighted mean copy number `τ = ∑ w q`, the weighted mean copy ratio is `1` (Carter et al. 2012, Methods: "correctly calibrated copy-ratio data always has mean = 1").
nodes.title: Calibrated copy ratios have mean `1`
